messages.content: It's extremely hot today and my air conditioner is currently turned off. Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour

function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Sends a command to control an appliance, allowing only a single value to be sent in one call. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing the parameters for the appliance command.

airConJobMode.description: The current job mode of the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength of the air flow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Whether air quality sensor monitoring is enabled.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning function.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air conditioner, indicating if it is turned on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Whether power save mode is enabled to conserve energy.

targetTemperature.description: The target temperature to set for the appliance, in degrees Celsius.

relativeHourToStop.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeMinuteToStop.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should stop. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to stop.

relativeHourToStart.description: The number of hours from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

relativeMinuteToStart.description: The number of minutes from the current time when the appliance should start. If set to null, the appliance will not be scheduled to start.

message.reasoning:
We need to parse user request: "Set it to start cooling at 20 degrees Celsius mid wind strength. power off after an hour". They want to turn on AC with cooling mode, target temp 20°C, wind strength mid, and schedule power off after an hour. Also they mention "mid wind strength" but the parameter is windStrength: "LOW" | "HIGH" | "MID". So we set windStrength: "MID". They want to start cooling at 20°C. They want to power off after an hour. That means relativeHourToStop: 1? But relativeMinuteToStop also can be used. They want to power off after an hour. So relativeHourToStop: 1, relativeMinuteToStop: 0. They didn't specify start time; presumably start immediately. So relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0? Or maybe we don't need to set start times; default is null meaning no schedule. But we want to start now. We can set relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0. But the function expects relativeHourToStart and relativeMinuteToStart as numbers or null. Setting 0 might mean start immediately. But we can also leave them null. But the user wants to start cooling now. So we can set relativeHourToStart: 0, relativeMinuteToStart: 0. Or we can just set airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON" to start now. The function has airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON" or "POWER_OFF". So we set airConOperationMode: "POWER_ON". Then we set relativeHourToStop: 1, relativeMinuteToStop: 0. Also set airConJobMode: "COOL". Set targetTemperature: 20. Set windStrength: "MID". Others default.

Thus we call ThinQ_Connect with body: {airConJobMode:"COOL", windStrength:"MID", airConOperationMode:"POWER_ON", targetTemperature:20, relativeHourToStop:1, relativeMinuteToStop:0}. Also we might set relativeHourToStart:0, relativeMinuteToStart:0 but not necessary. Let's include them for clarity: relativeHourToStart:0, relativeMinuteToStart:0. But the function may interpret 0 as immediate start. That seems fine.

Now produce the function call.
